nodes.text: He tells of deeds rightly done, furnishes the rising age with famous
examples, consoles the poor and the sick.
Along with the chaste boys, the girl who knows no husband —
where would she learn her prayers, if the Muse had not given a poet?
The chorus asks for help and feels the gods present;
it begs for rain from heaven, winning favour with the prayer it was taught;
it turns away diseases, drives off dreaded dangers,
obtains both peace and a year rich in harvests:
with song the gods above are appeased, with song the Manes [spirits of the dead].
The farmers of old, sturdy and happy with little,
when the grain was stored, refreshing at festival time
fled along with that vice? Is your breast free of empty
ambition? Free of the fear of death, and of anger?
ghosts that walk by night, and Thessalian portents — do you laugh at them?
Do you count your birthdays with gratitude? Do you forgive your friends?
Do you grow milder and better as old age draws on?
